steps.title: Prepare buffers and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions fresh before use as described: • Permeabilization buffer (50 mL): 15 mL 1 M sucrose, 2.5 mL 1 % Tween‑20, 0.5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 0.5 mL 0.1 M EGTA, 0.5 mL 10 % NP‑40, 0.25 mL 2 M KCl, 0.25 mL 1 M MgCl₂, 25 µL 1 M DTT, 5 µL SUPERase‑In, one protease‑inhibitor tablet, add DEPC‑water to 50 mL. • Storage buffer (800 µL): 0.2 µL 0.5 M EDTA, 10 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 5 µL 1 M MgCl₂, 5 µL 1 M DTT, 250 µL glycerol, 730 µL DEPC‑water. • 1 N NaOH: dissolve 2 g NaOH in 50 mL DEPC‑water. • Washing solution A (1 mL): 100 µL 1 N NaOH, 10 µL 5 M NaCl, 890 µL DEPC‑water; store 4 °C, 1 month. • Washing solution B (1 mL): 20 µL 5 M NaCl, 980 µL DEPC‑water; store 4 °C, 1 month. • 2× bead‑washing buffer (50 mL): 20 mL 5 M NaCl, 0.5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 5 mL 1 % Tween‑20, add DEPC‑water to 50 mL; store 4 °C, 1 month. • 1× bead‑washing buffer (50 mL): mix 25 mL 2× bead‑washing buffer with 25 mL DEPC‑water; store 4 °C, 1 month. • Pre‑washed streptavidin beads: add 170 µL Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 to a 1.5 mL tube, magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 500 µL washing solution A, wash once with 500 µL washing solution B, resuspend in 425 µL 2× bead‑washing buffer (use 50 µL for PRO‑seq).

steps.title: Collect and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Collect 1 × 10⁶–1 × 10⁸ cells in 20 mL ice‑cold PBS in a 50 mL tube, centrifuge 1 000 × g 5 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 20 mL ice‑cold permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 1 000 × g 5 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend in another 20 mL ice‑cold permeabilization buffer, incubate on ice 10 min, centrifuge 1 000 × g 5 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 500 µL storage buffer, aliquot into ten 1.5 mL tubes (≈50 µL each), flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (up to 1 week).

steps.title: Prepare 2× run‑on buffer
steps.instruction: Combine the following to make 2× run‑on buffer (final 1× after mixing with cells) and pre‑warm to 37 °C: 0.25 µL 1 M MgCl₂, 1 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 µL 0.1 M DTT, 7.5 µL 2 M KCl, 2 µL each of 1 mM Biotin‑11‑CTP, Biotin‑11‑UTP, Biotin‑11‑ATP, Biotin‑11‑GTP, 25 µL 2 % (w/v) Sarkosyl in DEPC‑water, 6.25 µL DEPC‑water, 1 µL RNase inhibitor. Adjust volumes proportionally for 8.5× stock if needed.

steps.title: Run‑on reactions (time‑course)
steps.instruction: Follow Table 2 exactly: for each labeled tube (32‑1, 32‑2, 8‑1, 8‑2, 2‑1, 2‑2, 0.5‑1, 0.5‑2) pre‑heat the stored cells at 37 °C at the indicated start time, add 50 µL pre‑warmed 2× run‑on buffer, mix by pipetting 15×. After the indicated incubation, add 500 µL TRIzol, vortex briefly, and place on ice. The schedule is: 0 min label 32‑1, 2 min label 32‑2, 4 min add buffer to 32‑1, 6 min add buffer to 32‑2, 8 min label 8‑1, 10 min label 8‑2, 12 min add buffer to 8‑1, 14 min add buffer to 8‑2, 20 min add TRIzol to 8‑1, 22 min add TRIzol to 8‑2, 24 min label 2‑1, 28 min add buffer to 2‑1, 30 min add TRIzol to 2‑1, 36 min add TRIzol to 32‑1, 38 min add TRIzol to 32‑2, 40 min label 2‑2, 44 min add buffer to 2‑2, 46 min add TRIzol to 2‑2, 48 min label 0.5‑1, 52 min add buffer to 0.5‑1, 52.5 min add TRIzol to 0.5‑1, 54 min label 0.5‑2, 58 min add buffer to 0.5‑2, 58.5 min add TRIzol to 0.5‑2.

steps.title: Post‑run‑on incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate all samples at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Phase separation with chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 130 µL chloroform to each tube, incubate RT 5 min, vortex vigorously 15 s. Transfer to 1.5 mL phase‑lock gel tubes (optional), incubate RT 5 min, centrifuge 14 000 × g 2 min at 4 °C, transfer the aqueous supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: RNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL GlycoBlue and an equal volume of isopropanol, vortex, incubate RT 10 min. Centrifuge 14 000 × g 20 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, dissolve RNA pellet in 30 µL DEPC‑water.

steps.title: RNA dephosphorylation
steps.instruction: Place RNA on ice, add 7.5 µL 1 N NaOH, incubate on ice 10 min.

steps.title: RNA cleanup and precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 37.5 µL pH 6.8 Tris‑HCl buffer, 125 µL DEPC‑water, 1 µL GlycoBlue, 8 µL 5 M NaCl, and 0.5 mL ice‑cold ethanol; vortex, centrifuge 16 000 × g 30 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, dissolve RNA in 6 µL DEPC‑water.

steps.title: 3′ adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL 20 µM 3′ RNA adapter, denature 65 °C 40 s, chill on ice. Add 13 µL ligation mix (Table 3): 2 µL 10× T4 RNA ligase buffer, 2 µL 10 mM ATP, 1 µL RNase inhibitor, 6 µL 50 % PEG8000, 2 µL T4 RNA ligase I, bring to 13 µL with DEPC‑water. Mix, incubate 25 °C 1 h (optional 20 °C 4 h).

steps.title: Capture ligated RNA on streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL DEPC‑water and 50 µL pre‑washed streptavidin beads to the ligation reaction, incubate RT 30 min with gentle rotation (10 rpm).

steps.title: Magnetic bead wash 1
steps.instruction: Place tubes on magnetic rack 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads with 500 µL 1× bead‑washing buffer, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare and add STP primer
steps.instruction: Mix 5 µL 100 µM STP with 170 µL DEPC‑water (20 µL for basic PRO‑seq), denature 95 °C 30 s, chill on ice. Add 20 µL denatured STP to beads, incubate RT 10 min with 10 rpm rotation.

steps.title: Magnetic bead wash 2
steps.instruction: Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads with 500 µL 1× bead‑washing buffer, discard supernatant.

steps.title: RppH treatment
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 20 µL RppH mix (Table 4): 16 µL DEPC‑water, 2 µL 10× ThermoPol buffer, 1 µL RppH, 1 µL SUPERase‑In. Incubate 37 °C 30 min.

steps.title: Magnetic bead wash 3
steps.instruction: Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads with 500 µL 1× bead‑washing buffer, discard supernatant.

steps.title: PNK treatment
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 20 µL PNK mix (Table 5): 14 µL DEPC‑water, 2 µL 10× PNK buffer, 2 µL 10 mM ATP, 1 µL T4 PNK, 1 µL SUPERase‑In. Incubate 37 °C 30 min.

steps.title: Magnetic bead wash 4
steps.instruction: Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads with 500 µL 1× bead‑washing buffer, discard supernatant.

steps.title: 5′ adapter ligation on beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 20 µL 5′ ligation mix (Table 6): 2 µL 10× T4 RNA ligase buffer, 2 µL 10 mM ATP, 1 µL RNase inhibitor, 6 µL 50 % PEG8000, 2 µL T4 RNA ligase I, 6 µL DEPC‑water, 1 µL 20 µM 5′ RNA adapter; mix, incubate 25 °C 1 h (optional 20 °C 4 h).

steps.title: Magnetic bead wash 5
steps.instruction: Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads with 500 µL 1× bead‑washing buffer, discard supernatant. Repeat wash once more (total two washes).

steps.title: Primer annealing for RT
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL 20 µM RP1 primer to beads, denature 95 °C 30 s, chill on ice.

steps.title: Reverse transcription premix addition
steps.instruction: Add 17 µL reverse‑transcription premix (Table 7): 10 µL 2× BioZues III RT buffer, 7 µL DEPC‑water. Then add 1 µL BioZues III RT enzyme and 1 µL RNase inhibitor, transfer the mixture to a PCR tube.

steps.title: Reverse transcription reaction
steps.instruction: Run on a thermocycler: 50 °C 10 min, 55 °C 10 min, hold 4 °C.

steps.title: PCR amplification of cDNA
steps.instruction: Add 31 µL NEBNext Ultra II Q5 Master Mix, 10 µL DEPC‑water, 1 µL 20 µM RPI‑n primer. Thermocycler program: 95 °C 10 min; 5 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 56 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; 10 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 65 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; 72 °C 10 min; hold 4 °C.

steps.title: AMPure XP bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 110 µL room‑temperature AMPure XP beads to the PCR reaction, mix, incubate RT 5 min. Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant. Wash beads twice with 70 % ethanol without resuspending. Air‑dry beads 5 min.

steps.title: Final library elution
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 22 µL 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0, incubate RT 5 min, place on magnet, transfer supernatant (final library) to a new tube for sequencing.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: • Jie Zhang et al. [14]. TV-PRO-seq reveals the pausing time of pausing sites at base pair resolution. This protocol is an enhanced version of our previous TV-PRO-seq (PRO-seq) protocol [14]. The two versions show a correlation exceeding 97% in the promoter-proximal regions of genes ( Figure 1 ). Figure 1. Fast TV-PRO-seq shows a strong correlation with the original TV-PRO-seq [14]. Comparison of promoter-proximal (TSS to +100 bp) read counts between original TV-PRO-seq (X-axis) and Fast TV-PRO-seq (Y-axis). The read counts exhibit a high degree of concordance between the two methods, as evidenced by a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.97.
